items.title: Workspace outbound access protection for Power BI semantic models and interactive reports (Generally Available)
items.summary: Workspace outbound access protection (OAP) is generally available for Power BI semantic models and interactive Power BI reports in Microsoft Fabric workspaces. With OAP, workspace admins can limit which data sources semantic models reach. They can also limit which semantic models in other workspaces interactive reports can query. These rules help reduce unintended outbound access and mitigate data exfiltration risks. Semantic model creators choose their data sources. Report authors choose their semantic models. Workspace admins decide which outbound connections they want to allow in their workspaces. You can have semantic models and reports in the same workspace if you don’t need strict governance controls. You can also place them in separate workspaces if you don’t want to give report authors direct access to the underlying data sources of the semantic models. Which workspace controls each connection An interactive report can always query a semantic model in its own local workspace. For a model in another workspace, however, the report workspace admin must add a Power BI Semantic Model exception to the report workspace’s OAP policy. Python scripts used in Power Query to populate tables are not affected. Power BI service: At retirement, all R and Python visuals will stop working in published reports, including those published before retirement. R-powered custom visuals: Custom visuals that use R will also no longer work at retirement. Older versions of Power BI Desktop: These visuals will continue to work locally using R and Python installed on your machine. Future versions of Power BI Desktop: After retirement, R and Python visuals will be removed, so you won't be able to add them to reports. What you need to do No migration within your report will recreate your exact R or Python visual. You must replace it with a different visualization before retirement.
